title: Ambiguous patch context placed session footer before final entries
description: Append-only log patches repeatedly used non-unique anchors: a repeated task block, an earlier matching record, a guessed timestamp, and finally a bare separator that placed a new session header at the beginning of the daily log.

context.code_snippet: @@ AGENT: Codex / TASK: Update mistake knowledge index / ... append SESSION ENDED

error_message: Session footer appeared at line 314 while later change entries continued through line 375.
root_cause: The patch used a duplicated nearby label instead of a unique final-entry context, so apply_patch selected an earlier valid match.
solution: Preserved every audit entry while relocating the collaboration block after the current session header, then switched final appends to unique latest-entry context and verified the physical file tail.

strategies: Use unique multi-line context when patching repeated structured logs
Inspect the tail of append-only files after finalization
Verify that session footers are the last records
code_patterns: Avoid: patch anchors made only from repeated labels
Use: anchors that include a unique timestamp or description
tests_to_add: Assert the final non-empty log block is SESSION ENDED

title: Session audit entries used projected future timestamps
description: Multiple conflict-review change entries used manually estimated timestamps that advanced beyond the actual system clock, making the session audit chronology inaccurate even though the recorded code changes were valid. The pattern recurred when a prior verified timestamp was reused for a later CSS patch instead of querying the clock again.
error_message: The final date check returned 2026-07-17 12:30:38 while the log contained entries through 12:55:42.
root_cause: Change batches were assigned plausible-looking manual times instead of querying the system clock at the point of each log update.
solution: Reconstructed a monotonic session timeline bounded by known Date.now markers from disposable fixtures and verification room slugs, corrected affected knowledge timestamps, and recorded the correction explicitly.

strategies: Run date immediately before every change-log patch
Never synthesize or project audit timestamps
Reject any final log entry later than the system clock
code_patterns: Avoid: manually incrementing timestamps between tool calls
tests_to_add: Validate session log timestamps are monotonic and no later than final wall clock

title: Plain room validation shadowed suffixed Yjs document routing
description: The first generalized Yjs parser tested the permissive room-slug pattern before inspecting the --pdf or --whiteboard suffix, so valid suffixed names were incorrectly classified as notes because double hyphens also satisfy the slug regex.
root_cause: The generic grammar was evaluated before the more specific suffix grammar, and the room regex intentionally permits consecutive hyphens.
solution: Parsed and validated the supported --pdf/--whiteboard suffixes first, then fell back to the plain notes-room form, and added direct parsing plus authenticated multi-channel persistence verification.

strategies: Evaluate specific routing grammars before permissive fallback patterns
Test every generated document name through both builder and parser
Verify each routed kind persists to its own database row
code_patterns: Avoid: checking a broad room pattern before tool suffixes
Use: parse supported suffix -> validate base slug -> fall back to plain notes
tests_to_add: Assert --pdf and --whiteboard names parse to their matching kinds
Open authenticated two-client providers for every document kind and assert durable row isolation

title: Version History trigger was interpreted as a floating panel instead of a toolbar action
description: The request to float Version History over the editor was implemented as a prominent floating accordion trigger. The user's Google Docs reference clarified that only the History icon belongs in the editor toolbar, with the panel opening below it.

context.code_snippet: <VersionHistoryPanel /> rendered as a large absolute trigger above <RichTextEditor />

error_message: User clarification: Add History icon on the right side of the toolbar, like Google Docs.
root_cause: The phrase 'float on top' was interpreted spatially without first mapping the requested interaction to the document-toolbar pattern shown in the reference.
solution: Moved the History trigger into the right side of EditorToolbar, controlled panel visibility from CollaborativeRoom, and retained only a right-aligned dropdown panel below the toolbar.

strategies: Treat named product references as interaction-pattern requirements, not only visual inspiration
Separate the placement of a feature trigger from the placement of its expanded content
Keep document-level actions such as history in the editor toolbar when a document-editor reference is provided
code_patterns: Avoid: a prominent floating trigger when the reference shows a compact toolbar action
Use: controlled toolbar button -> anchored overlay panel
tests_to_add: Assert the editor toolbar exposes a Version History button with aria-expanded and aria-controls
Assert toggling the toolbar button shows and hides the anchored history panel
